builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Bi-Phase Training: Learning Efficiently From Scratch
summary: BPT replaces full-parameter pre-training of a foundation model with a parameter-efficient update scheme: frozen base weights are adapted through trainable diagonal matrices and low-rank adapters composed with constrained high-rank left/right transformations, periodically merged back into the base. It reduces trainable-parameter memory and optimizer state during pre-training, but it still requires from-scratch pre-training on billions of tokens and does not claim to reduce total compute or data requirements to a single 24 GB GPU budget. It can fail through a residual perplexity and downstream-task gap versus full training, sensitivity to merge schedule and adapter constraints, and limited evidence beyond the reported model sizes, datasets, and token counts.
rationale: The method is relevant to efficient training, but adopting it would require the reader to pre-train models from scratch, which is outside the stated infrastructure and budget; it should be watched for future tooling or smaller-scale evidence rather than used in production now.

claims.statement: BPT replaces full-parameter pre-training of a foundation model with a parameter-efficient update scheme: frozen base weights are adapted through trainable diagonal matrices and low-rank adapters composed with constrained high-rank left/right transformations, periodically merged back into the base. It reduces trainable-parameter memory and optimizer state during pre-training, but it still requires from-scratch pre-training on billions of tokens and does not claim to reduce total compute or data requirements to a single 24 GB GPU budget. It can fail through a residual perplexity and downstream-task gap versus full training, sensitivity to merge schedule and adapter constraints, and limited evidence beyond the reported model sizes, datasets, and token counts.

At 1.5B scale, BPT uses 66% fewer trainable parameters than full-parameter pre-training (about 2.94x reduction) with only a small validation-perplexity gap; gains are reported on 100M-1.5B models trained on 10B-100B FineWeb-Edu tokens.
